acceptance_criteria: read_input raises HookInputError (a ValueError subclass) when stdin is not valid JSON.
read_input raises HookInputError (a ValueError subclass) when the parsed JSON is not a dict.
The HookInputError class definition in harness/hooks/_common.py is unchanged.
Existing behavior for empty/whitespace stdin (returning {}) and valid dict stdin is preserved.
Existing pytest test suite (including hooks unit tests and tests/adversarial/test_P1_scaffold.py, tests/adversarial/test_diff_fuzzer_structured.py, tests/adversarial/test_rebuild_p0_pins.py) passes.

edge_cases: Empty stdin or whitespace-only stdin: must still return {} without raising.
Valid dict payload: must still return the parsed dict unchanged.
Non-dict JSON value (list, scalar, null): must raise HookInputError, not bare ValueError.
Malformed JSON (truncated, invalid escapes, etc.): must raise HookInputError chaining the original JSONDecodeError.
functional_requirements: When stdin payload fails json.loads, read_input raises HookInputError with the original JSON decode error chained via `from exc`.
When the parsed JSON value is not a dict, read_input raises HookInputError with a message identifying the wrong type (e.g. 'hook stdin must be a JSON object, got list').
HookInputError remains a subclass of ValueError so existing `except ValueError` callers continue to handle these errors.
spec.implementation_notes: In harness/hooks/_common.py read_input (lines ~23-35): change `raise ValueError(f'hook stdin is not valid JSON: {exc}') from exc` to `raise HookInputError(f'hook stdin is not valid JSON: {exc}') from exc`, and change `raise ValueError(f'hook stdin must be a JSON object, got {type(data).__name__}')` to `raise HookInputError(...)` with the same message. No other code in the function or module should change.
spec.interfaces: read_input(stream=None) -> dict[str, Any] in harness/hooks/_common.py. HookInputError(ValueError) defined in the same module is unchanged.
non_goals: Do NOT modify the HookInputError class definition.
Do NOT modify _normalise_decision, decision_payload, or write_decision.
Do NOT alter the empty-stdin behavior that returns {}.
Do NOT touch any file other than harness/hooks/_common.py.
spec.objective: Replace the two `raise ValueError(...)` statements inside read_input (one for json.JSONDecodeError, one for non-dict payloads) with `raise HookInputError(...)`, so malformed stdin produces a typed exception subclass while remaining backwards-compatible with code that catches ValueError.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: io.StringIO streams containing: empty string, whitespace, valid JSON object, JSON list, JSON scalar, and a truncated/malformed JSON fragment.

claude_task.title: Raise HookInputError in read_input on malformed stdin

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is a two-line literal substitution (ValueError -> HookInputError) in one helper; the bulk of effort is exercising and asserting the new exception type without regressing the existing happy paths and adversarial suites.
